source_definition.value: Three categorical dieting-status groups: historical dieters, nondieters, and current dieters. Historical dieters reported at least two intentional efforts to lose weight but were not currently dieting; nondieters reported no history of weight-loss dieting; current dieters were dieting at scanning and had at least two prior intentional weight-loss efforts.

Categorical food-cue palatability condition. Highly palatable cues were french fries, pizza, chocolate cake, and ice cream; moderately palatable cues were an apple, white bread, carrots, and plain baked potato.

spans.text: Highly palatable cues were french fries, pizza, chocolate cake, and ice cream. Moderately palatable cues were an apple, a slice of white bread, carrots, and a plain baked potato.

description.value: Questionnaire assessing history of weight-loss dieting and current dieting status, used to classify participants as historical dieters, nondieters, or current dieters.
Abridged interview used to assess history of a diagnosed eating disorder for exclusion.
Questionnaire measuring hunger and fullness and confirming compliance with pre-study food-intake instructions.
Restraint subscale of the Three-Factor Eating Questionnaire measuring cognitive dietary restraint.
Fast randomized event-related fMRI task presenting highly palatable food, moderately palatable food, neutral, and romantic photographic cues in fasted and fed scanning blocks.

instructions.value: Participants were instructed not to eat or drink for 8 hours before the study visit, apart from water.

stimuli.value: Color photographs displayed on a rear-projection screen and viewed through a mirror mounted on the head coil; each cue was presented for 500 ms with a 1.5 s interstimulus interval.
